rationale: A boilerplate toString override on the Owner entity that formats its fields with ToStringCreator. It is a trivial formatting helper with no callers and no architectural role, so it would not be modelled as an element.

Private helper in OwnerController that builds a fixed-size PageRequest and delegates to the repository query. It is an implementation detail of processFindForm, below modelling granularity. Persistence itself happens in OwnerRepository, so this method only calls it.

A private helper that copies pagination values into the Spring MVC model and returns the view name. It is an implementation detail of showVetList and not an architectural element on its own. It prepares view data but does not render a user interface itself.

A small domain method on the Owner entity that validates its arguments, looks up a pet and delegates to Pet.addVisit. It does no persistence or I/O itself. This is an entity-level implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element; the Owner entity would be modelled instead.

This is a Spring Data repository query method that reads Vet records from the data store in pages. It is transactional and cached. As a repository read operation it is evidence of a data-store access pattern. It is notable but is a single method within VetRepository.

Boilerplate override of Spring's Validator.supports that performs a one-line type check for Pet. It is an implementation detail of PetValidator, not an architectural element on its own, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Spring @InitBinder boilerplate that stops request binding from setting 'id' fields, a small mass-assignment safeguard. This is a simple accessor on the Vet entity that returns its specialties sorted by name, with an @XmlElement serialization annotation. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element itself. The Vet entity would be modelled, not this getter.

A trivial accessor that returns the name field of the NamedEntity base class. It is an implementation detail with no behaviour of its own. The data-model element is the entity itself, not this getter.

A Spring Data repository query method that retrieves an Owner by id from the database. It is a documented, widely used read access pattern on the owner store, called by multiple controllers. It is a notable data-access unit rather than a standalone component, and it implements data persistence.

Trivial setter on the Visit entity. It only assigns a field and has no behaviour of its own. Accessors are below the granularity of an architecture element; the Visit entity itself would be modelled, not its setters.

Pet is a JPA entity and a core domain object. It defines birthDate, its PetType association and its visits collection. It is best modelled as a data-model object schema. The ORM mapping to the pets table is evidence for a separate data-store collection, but the class itself performs no I/O.

Trivial getter on the Person entity that simply returns a field. Accessors are below the granularity of an architectural element. The Person entity itself would be modelled in data-model, but this method is an implementation detail with no behaviour or cross-cutting concern.

JPA entity Visit is a core domain entity of PetClinic. It carries fields (date, description) with validation constraints, which makes it a logical data-model object schema. The @Table mapping is declarative and the class performs no storage I/O itself, so data_persistence is false.

Trivial JavaBean setter on the Person entity. It holds no behaviour beyond field assignment. Accessors fall below the granularity at which architectural elements are modelled, so it is not an element on its own; the Person entity itself would be the data-model element.

HTTP GET /oups route handler in Spring PetClinic. It deliberately throws an exception to showcase error-page handling. It is an exposed endpoint, so it is modelled as an API operation, but it is a demo endpoint of modest significance.

Spring bean factory method that configures a framework LocaleChangeInterceptor to read a 'lang' parameter. A Spring MVC controller exposing a single demo endpoint (/oups) that throws an exception to showcase error-page handling. It is a mounted controller access point, so it is modelled as an application interface, but it exists for demonstration purposes and has minimal architectural significance.

A trivial Spring Formatter method that renders a PetType as its name string, falling back to "<null>". It is a formatting helper below the granularity of an architecture element, so it has no layer and no cross-cutting concerns.

A one-line Spring MVC configuration override that registers the locale change interceptor. It is framework wiring boilerplate inside WebConfiguration, not an element a maintainer would model on its own. The configuration class itself would be the element, if anything.

Trivial getter on the Visit entity that returns a field. Accessors are below the granularity of an architecture element. The Visit entity itself may be modelled in the data-model layer, but this method is not an element on its own.

Trivial setter on the Owner entity that only assigns a field. Accessors are implementation details below the modelling granularity. The Owner entity itself would be the data-model element, not this method.

A trivial accessor on the Owner entity that returns the telephone field. Accessors fall below the granularity rule. The telephone attribute would be modelled as a schema property of the Owner entity, not as a separate element.

A trivial setter on the Pet entity that only assigns a field. Accessors fall below the model's granularity rule. The Pet entity itself would be the data-model element, not its setters, and this method implements no cross-cutting concern.

A Spring Validator that enforces the Pet form's business validation rules: name required with a maximum length, type required for new pets, and birth date required. Constructor of VetController that only assigns the injected VetRepository dependency. This is dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The controller class is the architectural element; its constructor is an implementation detail.

Spring Data repository interface defining read access to Vet records (findAll, paged findAll) with transactional and cache annotations. It is the persistence access layer for vets, so it is best modelled as a data-store access pattern. It is significant as the store interface for a core aggregate.

GraalVM native-image runtime hints registrar. This is build/runtime configuration boilerplate that registers resource patterns and reflection types. It is not an architectural element a maintainer would model, though it relates loosely to native-image deployment.

Framework callback that registers GraalVM native-image resource and reflection hints. It is build and runtime configuration boilerplate, not an architectural element. Spring configuration that enables JCache caching and creates the 'vets' cache with statistics exposed over JMX. It is infrastructure/platform setup, a caching technology service consumed by the application. It is moderately significant and touches caching (persistence) and statistics (observability).

This is a private helper that builds a JCache MutableConfiguration with statistics enabled, and its only caller is the cache customizer bean. It is an implementation detail of CacheConfiguration, the class that would be modelled, and is not an element on its own.

A trivial collection mutator on the Pet entity that appends a Visit to its in-memory visits list. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element on its own. Persistence happens elsewhere, via JPA cascade or the repository.

A Spring MVC @Controller mounted at /owners/{ownerId}. It is the HTTP access point for pet create and update forms: it binds and validates form input, delegates storage to the injected repositories, and returns server-rendered view names. That makes it a mounted controller interface rather than a pure API contract. It drives the web UI, while persistence is delegated to the repositories.

A Spring MVC @Controller that serves the vets HTML page, with pagination, and a JSON vets resource. As the access point exposing vet-listing behaviour over HTTP, it is an ApplicationInterface. It drives the UI by populating the view model. Persistence is delegated to VetRepository.

A trivial setter on the Person entity that only assigns a field. Accessors fall below the charter's granularity rule, so this is not an architectural element. The Person entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer; this method would not.

Trivial derived accessor on the Vet entity that returns the size of its specialties collection. It is an implementation detail below the architectural granularity threshold, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A trivial getter on the Pet entity that returns the visits collection. It is an accessor, so under the granularity rule it is not an architectural element. The Pet entity and its visits relationship would be modelled at the class level in the data-model layer instead.

A Spring @InitBinder configuration hook that attaches PetValidator and disallows binding of id fields. It is framework wiring inside PetController, not an element a maintainer would model separately. The validator and the controller are the meaningful elements.

A Spring MVC handler bound to GET /owners. It implements the owner search operation: it normalises the last-name query, paginates the results and either redirects or picks the view to render. A trivial setter on the Owner entity. It holds no behaviour beyond assigning a field, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element. The Owner entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, not this accessor.

A Spring MVC GET /owners/find handler that returns the find-owners view name. As an HTTP route handler it is best modelled as an API operation. It is simple, with no logic beyond selecting the view, so its significance is moderate. It drives the UI by choosing which template renders.

A trivial @ModelAttribute helper inside VisitController that supplies tomorrow's date to the view model, likely as a form minimum. It has no logic beyond a date calculation and sits below the granularity at which an architecture model records elements.

HTTP POST route /owners/new is an API operation contract on the system boundary for creating owners. Its handler validates the form, persists via the repository (owners.save) and returns an MVC view or redirect, so it drives the web UI and writes durable storage.

Trivial collection mutator on the Vet entity that appends a Specialty to an internal set. This is an accessor-level implementation detail of the data-model entity, not an architectural element. It does no persistence itself; JPA handles that elsewhere.

A Spring MVC GET handler bound to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit. It only returns the pet create-or-update form view name, with the pet supplied by a model attribute elsewhere. It is modelled as an API operation of moderate significance, and it drives the UI by selecting which view renders.

A private helper inside VetController. It builds a PageRequest and delegates to VetRepository.findAll. This is pagination plumbing below modelling granularity. It does not touch storage itself, so data_persistence is false; the repository does that work.

Spring Data derived query method on OwnerRepository that reads owners from the database by last-name prefix with pagination. It represents a documented data access pattern used by the owner search controller. It is a notable query in the persistence layer, not a standalone component.

A Spring @Bean factory method that configures a session-based locale resolver defaulting to English. It is framework wiring boilerplate for i18n, not an element a maintainer would name in an architecture model. The parent WebConfiguration class could be modelled, but this method on its own is not.

A protected lazy-initializing accessor on the Vet entity that returns the specialties set, creating it if null. It is a trivial internal helper used only by sibling accessors in the same class, so it has no architectural meaning on its own.

Owner is a core JPA domain entity with validated properties (address, city, telephone) and a one-to-many relationship to Pet. It is an entity/schema definition, so it belongs in data-model as an object schema. The mapping annotations describe persistence, but the class performs no storage I/O itself.

HTTP GET / route in Spring MVC WelcomeController returning the 'welcome' view name. It is an HTTP operation binding on the server surface and the application's landing entry point, but trivial in behaviour. It drives the user-facing welcome page render, so user_interface applies.

A JPA @MappedSuperclass that adds a validated name property to BaseEntity. It is a shared domain base schema that entities such as PetType and Specialty inherit. It defines data shape, not behaviour, so it fits the data-model layer as an object schema of moderate significance. The class itself does no persistence I/O.

Vets is a simple JAXB-annotated wrapper around a list of Vet, used as a response payload for XML/JSON marshalling. It has no behaviour beyond a lazy accessor, so it is a passive data object. It is a minor unit used by a single controller method.

HTTP GET /vets route returning a JSON/XML Vets resource via @ResponseBody. It is a public API operation in the petclinic REST surface. It reads vets through the repository, but persistence is delegated to VetRepository, so the symbol does not itself implement data persistence.

isNew is a trivial accessor on BaseEntity that only checks whether the id is null. It is an implementation detail of the entity base class, not an architectural element in its own right. It does no persistence work itself and has no cross-cutting concerns.

Spring @Configuration class wiring i18n: a session-based locale resolver and a request interceptor for ?lang switching. It is a notable configuration component a maintainer would name when explaining localization support. It drives the user-facing language, but it is framework wiring rather than a UI view.

JPA @MappedSuperclass defining the shared identity property (id) for all petclinic entities. It is a domain entity schema base, so it belongs in the data-model layer as an object schema. It is a notable base abstraction, but it performs no persistence I/O itself; the JPA annotations are only declarative mapping.

This is a JPA @Entity mapped to the 'specialties' table, representing the Vet specialty domain entity. It inherits id and name from NamedEntity and adds no behaviour, so it is best modelled as a data-model object schema. It is a notable but small domain entity.

Spring MVC @Controller that exposes the visit-booking HTTP endpoints and drives server-rendered form views. It drives the UI by returning view names, form validation errors and flash messages.

PetType is a JPA @Entity domain type (mapped to the 'types' table) representing a pet category such as cat or dog. It is a domain entity definition with no behaviour, so it is best modelled as a data-model object schema. It is a notable but small entity in the model.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId} is an API operation exposed by OwnerController. It renders the ownerDetails view via ModelAndView, so it drives the UI. It loads the owner through the repository rather than persisting data itself. It is a significant endpoint in the petclinic surface.

HTTP POST route for editing a pet is an API operation at the system boundary. It validates form input, delegates the persistence update to a helper, and drives the MVC UI by returning a view name or a redirect with a flash message. Persistence is done by callees, not by this handler.

A Spring MVC GET handler for /vets.html. As a route handler it maps to an API operation. It validates the page number, redirects when out of range, and populates the model for a server-rendered view, so it drives a user-facing UI. Persistence is delegated to findPaginated.

A @ModelAttribute method in a Spring MVC controller that preloads the owner and pet and builds a new Visit before each request handler runs. It is internal controller plumbing behind the visit endpoints, not an endpoint itself. It calls the repository but does no persistence work of its own, so it is a minor application function.

Constructor that only assigns an injected PetTypeRepository to a field. It is dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, so it is not an architectural element. The enclosing PetTypeFormatter class would be the element to model, not its constructor.

POST route handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new: the primary endpoint for booking a visit. It validates the date, persists the owner via the repository, and drives the MVC UI by returning views, redirects and flash messages. Best modelled as an API operation.

This Spring @Bean registers a JCache customizer that creates the 'vets' cache. It is infrastructure configuration for the caching platform service, not business logic. It is notable but small, so significance is 2. It configures the cache rather than reading or writing cached data, so no persistence concern is flagged.

A Spring MVC @Controller that maps GET / to the server-rendered 'welcome' view. It is a web access point (controller binding) rather than a JSON API contract or business logic. It is trivial, a single landing-page handler, so its significance is modest. It selects a UI view, so it drives the user interface.

This is the core validation behaviour of PetValidator. It enforces the pet name (required, at most 30 characters), type and birth-date rules for form binding. It is an internal application function owned by the validator component, notable within the owner module but not an exposed service. It touches no cross-cutting concerns.

HTTP GET route in Spring MVC OwnerController that serves the owner edit form view. As an HTTP endpoint it is modelled as an API operation. It returns a server-rendered view name, so it drives the user interface. It is a notable but ordinary endpoint in the petclinic owner module.

An HTTP POST route that handles submission of the new-visit form, so it is an API operation. The handler validates the visit date, saves the owner through the repository, and returns a view name or redirect with a flash message. That gives it persistence and user-interface concerns, and it is a core user-facing endpoint.

GET /oups is an HTTP route, so it is modelled as an API operation. It exists only to demonstrate error handling by throwing a RuntimeException and has no business behaviour, so its architectural significance is minor. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity that returns its type field. Accessors fall below the granularity at which the architecture model records elements. The Pet entity itself would be the data-model element; this method has no behaviour or cross-cutting concern of its own.

A Spring MVC POST handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new, which makes it an HTTP operation in the API surface. It validates the form input, persists the owner and new pet via saveAndFlush, and drives the UI by returning view names, redirects and flash messages. It is a primary entry point for the add-pet use case.

Entity method on the Owner aggregate that adds a pet to the in-memory collection with duplicate checks. It is minor domain behaviour inside a JPA entity. It does no I/O itself, since persistence happens via the repository, so it ranks as a minor internal application function.

Trivial toString override on the NamedEntity base class that returns the name or a placeholder. It is a formatting helper below the granularity of any architecture element. The listed callers are mostly unrelated toString resolutions from the call graph.

Default constructor of the Visit entity that initialises the visit date to tomorrow. It is a trivial constructor and an implementation detail of the data-model entity. It is not an architectural element on its own, and it touches no cross-cutting concerns.

Vet is a JPA entity and core domain object (a veterinarian with a many-to-many set of specialties). As an entity class describing domain data, it maps to a data-model object schema; its table mapping is evidence for the data-store layer. It holds no logic beyond accessors, so data_persistence is false: the repository does the actual storage.

HTTP GET /owners route: an API operation searching owners by last name with pagination and redirects. It is a system boundary endpoint in an MVC app. It drives UI by selecting views and redirects. Persistence is delegated to a helper/repository, so it is not flagged here.

A trivial getter on the Owner entity that returns the city field. Accessors are implementation details and not architectural elements. The owning Owner entity or its city property would be modelled in data-model instead.

A trivial getter on the Person entity that returns a field. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architecture model. The lastName property would be modelled on the Person schema itself, not as this method.

Trivial setter on the Visit entity, which only assigns a field. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architecture element. The Visit entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, not this method.

Standard Spring Boot main method boilerplate that only delegates to SpringApplication.run. The architecturally meaningful element is the PetClinicApplication component itself, not this one-line bootstrap method, so it is scaffolding below modelling granularity.

This is the constructor of VisitController and only performs dependency injection, assigning the OwnerRepository field. That is boilerplate wiring with no behaviour of its own. The controller class is the modelled element; its constructor is not.

A Spring Formatter parse method that converts form text into a PetType by looking it up through the repository. Spring Data JPA repository for PetType. It is the persistence access layer and defines a custom JPQL query that reads pet types ordered by name. That makes it a data-store access pattern. It is a small lookup repository, so it rates as a notable internal unit rather than a core store.

A trivial lazy-initializing accessor on the Vets JAXB wrapper DTO. The @XmlElement annotation only shapes serialization. The method is an implementation detail of the data object rather than an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A trivial getter on the Pet entity that returns a field. It is an accessor, not an architectural element. The Pet entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, but this method is below the granularity cut-off.

An HTTP GET route on the PetClinic MVC controller that returns the visit-creation form view. It is an endpoint on the system's HTTP surface, so it is modelled as an api operation. Its significance is moderate because it only renders a form template, which also makes it a user-interface concern.

A Spring MVC handler bound to GET / that returns the 'welcome' Thymeleaf view name. As an HTTP route handler it maps to an API operation. It is the application's landing page, so it is notable, but it is trivial with no logic. It drives the user-facing page by selecting the view to render.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new exposed by Spring MVC PetController. It is an API operation that initializes a new Pet and returns the create/update form view name, so it drives the web UI. Trivial setter on the NamedEntity base entity class. It is an accessor with no behaviour beyond assigning a field, so it is below the granularity of an architectural element. The owning entity, not this method, would be modelled in the data-model layer.
